dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel mentioned you previously, honored guest. Please, have a look around.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Hmm? You've got a good eye, I must say. Yes, I am indeed a merchant. I sell the various things that the tribe lacks. Cosmetics, luxury items, costumes, toys, agricultural products, intricate tools...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: What would you like? If you should need something, I'll have it. And if I don't, just tell me what you need, and I'll get it for you, whether it's from the city, or even from Fontaine!

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Ah... Right, you're an outsider. Well, in that case, you have my apologies, but my shop is not open to you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've got lots of books here. May I read them?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: The books? Oh! Right, those are here at the request of Matriarch Babel. I'm sure you've heard, and seen, that the city people have taken to using this thing called the Akasha, which they mount on their ears.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Their libraries have been emptied of a great number of obsolete books, and the Matriarch had me purchase and safe-keep them for everyone to read free of charge. Hmph... I operated at a loss there.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: As for the Akasha, we did ship a set in from another tribe, but it was... very inconvenient to use, not to mention quite arcane indeed. We could not disassemble or repair it, for the wiring was too centralized...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Whatever the case, I'd say that reading books on your own is far better than relying on some strange machine to stuff information into your brain.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: After all, who knows what back doors you might open if you just let people into the door of your mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Don't let me get in your way.

choices.text: What are you selling here, anyway?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Straight to the point, hmm? I like buyers like you. Unfortunately, I don't sell to outsiders.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Um, this is not due to xenophobia or some kind of base prejudice. It's more that... Our tribe and the merchants in the cities don't share economic spheres, if you can glean my meaning?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I only serve the Tanit tribe, you know, as our exclusive distributer of goods. All trade and other transactions have to go through Matriarch Babel, and I take a small cut of that.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Benben... Ah, you mean the little machine that follows Jeht around.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I've examined it before. There's nothing particularly wrong with it, but as for how it can be restored to its former, energetic state...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I have my ways... but I don't think I could tell you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Whatever the case, I think it's best that it stays with me till the repairs are done.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Anything else you'd like to ask me?
